html:
Sir Francis Drake was an English sea captain, privateer and slave trader under Elizabeth I. He led the first voyage round the world that its commander survived, from 1577 to 1580, and helped beat the Spanish Armada in 1588.

Born in Devon around 1540, he learned the sea on slaving voyages with his cousin John Hawkins in the 1560s, carrying captured Africans to sell in the Spanish Caribbean. After a Spanish attack on their ships in Mexico in 1568, he spent his life raiding Spain's empire, with the queen's quiet backing. In 1573, helped by escaped Africans, the Cimarrones, he seized a silver train in Panama.

On his voyage round the world in the Golden Hind he passed through the strait found by Magellan, raided the Pacific coast of Chile and Peru, and took a Spanish treasure ship. In 1579 he landed in California, most likely among the Coast Miwok north of the Golden Gate (see Graton Rancheria), and claimed the land as Nova Albion. The queen knighted him on his ship in 1581.

In 1585 and 1586 he raided Cidade Velha in Cape Verde and sacked Santo Domingo and Cartagena. In 1587 he burned Spanish ships at Cádiz. He died of dysentery off Panama in 1596, on a failed raid, and was buried at sea. To the English he was a hero; to the Spanish he was El Draque, a pirate.
sum: Sir Francis Drake was an English sea captain, privateer and slave trader under Elizabeth I. He led the first voyage round the world that its commander survived, from 1577 to 1580, and helped beat the Spanish Armada in 1588.
